text: rwb-source-data extracts the legacy Workbench document and document field records for the open cases and hands them over as a file with a checksum and per-entity counts; rwb-document loads them into rwb_document on its own Flyway sequence; rwb-case holds recovery_case. rwb_source_data holds no document, document field or custody table, and this story's version creates none.
why: RWB-DM-010 says 'migrated from the legacy Workbench' without naming the service that holds the records after D-RCV-60, and no source gives the dump, the handover location or the retention period. The Ownership Map puts document, document_field and document_custody with P5 rwb-document and recovery_case with P3 rwb-case, and DP-01 forbids a service writing another service's schema.
read: _work/msr/context/P1.md (service row, 18 owned tables, DP table); FSD P1 v3 A2.2 (DP10); TSD P1 v3 T3.6, T3.2; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-01, DP-15 and §R9
confirm: Data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW) with the rwb-document service owner at the wave 4 entry check
impact: The extract is a file and not a table, the load is P5's story, and the story's own version is a no-op on the schema. If P1 were instead to hold the tables, the story would need a document table, a custody table and a load path that this document does not describe.

text: The extract carries storage_ref character for character and no document content; no OCR, scan, classification, upload or re-extraction runs at migration, and the WORM custody of the content stays with rwb-document, which adopts the carried reference in its own custody record on load.
why: Legacy AC1 states 'no document is re-extracted and no scan is repeated at migration' and the legacy guardrails say a migrated record never holds a copy of an ACE row. No source states what a storage_ref points at or who owns the Blob object during the cutover window.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-010 AC1 and guardrails; FSD P1 v3 A2.2 (DP10); _work/msr/context/P1.md (no data lake, DP-05, DP-15)
confirm: rwb-document service owner at the wave 4 entry check
impact: No content is read into the extract, a log, a test or a prompt; a document whose reference names no object is listed for rwb-document rather than fetched or re-uploaded here.

text: The cutover evidence is ten consecutive business dates whose reconciliation_result rows are PASS with no unexplained variance and no new REC-05 orphan on a migrated record; a break resets the count. The count is derived each run from those rows and no counter table is created, and the data steward's sign-off is held in the cutover record of the release pipeline, not in a Workbench table.
why: Legacy AC3 requires 'ten clean days on the migrated records' and a sign-off, and names no table, no report and no holder of the count. The reconciliation that produces the rows is JOB-04 of RWB-P1-E1011-APP, and this story must not duplicate it.
read: Legacy RWB-DM-010 AC3; FSD P1 v3 A2.11; TSD P1 v3 T3.6 (reconciliation_result, REC-05), T5.3; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-15
confirm: Data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW) at the wave 4 entry check
impact: A BREAK result or a new REC-05 orphan resets the count and the date is listed; a stale ACE batch is never a clean day; the sign-off leaves no table behind.

text: Legacy AC2 Reconcile the business keys and its REC-05 break list belong to RWB-ITG-DM010-ITG, which owns AC2 as its AC1 and carries the ITG copies TC-DM-010-01-ITG to TC-DM-010-04-ITG. This story owns AC1 and AC3 only and reads the reconciliation_result rows that AC2's step writes, without asserting the cross-service key resolution itself.
why: The WP gives this story AC1 and AC3. RWB-DM-010 AC2 asserts that every business key on a migrated record resolves to its view row, which is cross-service behaviour and belongs on an ITG story under §R5.4 (class I).
read: _work/msr/fragments/RWB-ITG-DM010-ITG.json (AC1 origin legacy RWB-DM-010 AC2, I RWB-P1-DM010-APP); Template and Rules v1 §R5.4, §R7.2 s7 and s16
confirm: Integration story owner RWB-ITG-DM010-ITG at the wave 4 entry check
impact: No AC2 text is copied into this story; TC-DM-010-02 is kept at Component level as the read of the REC-05 rows AC3 counts, and the cross-service assertion stays with the ITG story.
